title: Applied ML & Evals: Unified Guidelines, Playbooks, and Standards
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document defines the unified guidelines and playbooks for Applied ML and Evals at Redwood Inference. It consolidates standards for the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profile selection, and regression triage. The goal is to provide a single reference that engineering, applied ML, and product teams can follow to reliably onboard models, detect regressions, and keep production quality within defined thresholds.

Scope and audience

- Scope: eval harness development, prompt set curation, benchmark methodology, onboarding checklist, guardrail definitions, quantization profile selection, regression detection and triage.
- Audience: ML engineers, SREs, platform engineers, product managers, and solutions engineers.

Ownership and roles

- Primary owner: Applied ML (engineering).
- Secondary owners: Eng-platform (tooling), Eng-serving-runtime (performance/latency validation), Eng-SRE (SLOs & monitoring).
- Reviewers: Applied ML, Security (for data-sensitive workloads), Product for rollout criteria.

High-level principles

1. Reproducibility: every eval must be versioned (model + prompt set + harness commit + dataset seed).
2. Observability: all evals publish token-level metrics, latency breakdowns, and cost estimates to Redwood Console dashboards.
3. Developer ergonomics: harness APIs must be simple, well-documented, and provide canonical adapters for local and CI execution.
4. Production-first: guardrails and regression detection are mandatory for any model promoted to Hosted or Dedicated.

1) Eval Harness standards

Purpose: provide a single executable environment for running unit, integration, and longitudinal evals against candidate models and model variants.

Minimum requirements:
- Source control: harness code + runner configs must be in git with a TAGABLE release (semver-like).
- Config-driven: YAML-run configs that specify model id, model commit/sha, dataset(s), prompt-sets, quantization profile, and runtime settings.
- Deterministic seeds: default RNG seeds for sampling to ensure reproducible comparisons.
- CI integration: smoke tests for regressions run on PRs; nightly full-suite runs for baseline models.

Example run command:
```
# Run full eval locally (example)
poetry run ri-eval run --config configs/llama-variant/full-suite.yaml --output results/2029-02-28/
```

Canonical outputs produced by harness:
- metrics.csv (per-example metrics)
- aggregated.json (summary metrics and CI-like pass/fail flags)
- logs.tar.gz (runtime logs + kernel traces for perf regressions)

2) Prompt sets & benchmark guidelines

Purpose: ensure prompt sets reflect real customer workloads and edge cases for quality evaluation and regression detection.

Curation rules:
- Ownership: every prompt set must have an owner (team/person) and documented provenance.
- Metadata: each prompt must include intent, expected outputs (gold/soft labels), difficulty, and tags (safety, hallucination-risk, context-length, domain).
- Diversity: prompt sets must include short and long context, multi-turn chat scenarios, and adversarial variants. Aim for 20-40% edge/adversarial examples per critical benchmark.
- Size and splits: canonical prompt sets should have train/validation/holdout splits where applicable. For black-box regression checks, maintain a stable holdout (no modifications) for at least 12 months.

Benchmarking methodology:
- Metric taxonomy: accuracy/EM for closed tasks, F1/precision/recall for extraction, BLEU/ROUGE for generation where applicable, and custom correctness checks implemented as unit-style evaluators.
- Quality signals: correctness, reasoning-chain integrity (when chain-of-thought is used), hallucination-rate, and instruction-following score.
- Reliability metrics: per-token perplexity, expected-next-token likelihood distribution, and calibration histograms.
- Performance signals: median and p95 latency at representative batch sizes, and per-token cost estimate (USD/token).

Example prompt metadata (JSON example stored in repo):
```
{
  "prompt_id": "support-faq-0001",
  "intent": "answer-faq",
  "expected": "short factual answer",
  "difficulty": "low",
  "tags": ["faq", "low-context"]
}
```

3) Model onboarding guide (step-by-step)

Purpose: provide a checklist and acceptance criteria to move a model from prototype to production (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).

Onboarding checklist (numbered):
1. Initial offline evals: run the eval harness against benchmark suite and collect aggregate metrics. Document versions.
2. Safety & PII scan: run static prompt-scan and model-output scanning against our safety rules and PII detectors.
3. Quantization candidate selection: run quantization profiles (see section 5) and compare quality/perf tradeoffs.
4. Performance validation: measure throughput and latency on representative infra (sequence-length distributions representative of target workload). Target numbers: median token-latency <= 40ms for typical interactive workloads; p95 <= 200ms under expected load (these targets are workload-dependent and must be set in the PRD).
5. Canary deploy: deploy model to canary slice (5% traffic) with automated rollback on any SLO/quality threshold breach.
6. Observability hooks: ensure token-level cost reporting, per-route dashboards, and tracing are enabled.
7. SLA & documentation: prepare model README, supported capabilities, failure modes, and recommended quantization profiles.

Acceptance criteria (all must be satisfied):
- No critical safety violations from scanner.
- Holdout benchmark delta within allowed thresholds (see "Regression thresholds").
- Latency and cost fall within expected ranges for target deployment tier.

4) Quality guardrails (automated + human-in-loop)

Guardrail categories:
- Automated checks: prompt-level correctness rules, hallucination detectors, toxicity filters, and PII redaction checks. These run in the harness and in production inference path for monitored customers.
- Statistical checks: rolling-window checks against holdout metrics, alerting on >3% absolute drop in instruction-following score or >5% relative increase in hallucination rate.
- Human review: weekly sampling of produced outputs for new model variants or major changes (at least 200 samples/week for high-traffic models).

Guardrail failure actions:
1. Auto-rollback (critical severity): immediate rollback to previous model variant. Triggered by safety policy failures or severe metric regression (pre-configured).
2. Canary throttling (high severity): reduce canary traffic to zero and notify on-call.
3. Investigation (medium): open a regression triage ticket and assign to owner.

5) Quantization profiles and guidance

Purpose: define supported quantization configurations and recommended selection criteria to balance cost vs quality.

Profile naming convention: {precision}-{grouping}-{backend} e.g. q4_0-g8-tensorrt or q2_k-cuda.

Recommended starting profiles (guidelines):
- Small models (<1B params): fp16 to preserve quality; only quantize for memory-constrained Private deployments.
- Medium models (1B-7B): q4_0 or q4_k recommended for a good quality/cost balance.
- Large models (7B-30B): q4_k with careful eval; q3/q2 options for aggressive cost optimization but require stronger guardrails.
- LLMs >30B: prefer mixed-precision fp16 for correctness-critical workloads; aggressive quantization only after extensive eval.

Quantization evaluation checklist:
- Run full eval harness for each profile. Compare per-task metrics to float baseline.
- Identify categories with >2% absolute accuracy drop or >5% relative hallucination increase as candidates for rejection.
- Run end-to-end latency and memory profiling on target hardware. Document memory reduction and cost savings.

Config snippet (example YAML):
```
quantization:
  profile: q4_k-cuda
  block_size: 128
  calibration_samples: 2000
  per_channel: true
```

6) Regression detection & triage playbook

Detection sources:
- CI harness runs (PR-level and nightly).
- Production monitors: rolling-window holdout checks, A/B canary comparisons, and user-reported incidents.
- Manual audits and random sampling.

Initial triage steps (numbered):
1. Triage ticket: create a ticket in Jira with model id, deploy id, timestamps, and attached harness outputs.
2. Verify signal: reproduce the regression locally against the stable holdout. If irreproducible, mark as flaky and schedule re-run.
3. Categorize: quality (semantic correctness), safety (policy violation), perf (latency/memory), or infra (kernel/fp errors).
4. Prioritize: use the matrix below to set urgency.

Prioritization matrix (impact x severity)
- High impact + critical severity -> Pager and rollback.
- High impact + major severity -> High priority ticket, war-room.
- Medium impact -> Investigate within team business day.
- Low impact -> Schedule in next sprint.

Root cause analysis checklist:
- Compare token-level deltas between baseline and candidate.
- Inspect kernel traces and perf logs for scheduler or memory contention issues.
- Check quantization profile differences and calibration artifacts.
- Verify any prompt-set changes or data drift in customer traffic.

Communication and SLAs:
- For critical regressions affecting production, notify stakeholders via PagerDuty + #incidents channel within 15 minutes.
- Postmortem: publish a 72-hour interim update and a full write-up within 7 business days if the regression triggered a rollback or significant customer impact.

Operational dashboards and alerts

Minimum dashboards to maintain:
- Model health: holdout pass-rate, hallucination-rate, instruction-following score across versions.
- Performance: median/p95 latency, throughput, and per-token cost.
- Safety: any PII/safety detections and policy violations with trend lines.

Alert thresholds (examples):
- Holdout pass-rate drop > 3 percentage points -> SEV3 alert.
- Hallucination-rate increase > 5% relative -> SEV2 alert.
- p95 latency increase > 50% from baseline -> SEV2 alert.

Appendices

A. Example model onboarding PR template (checklist)
- Model ID:
- Baseline commit/sha:
- Harness run link:
- Holdout metrics (baseline vs candidate):
- Quantization profiles tested:
- Canary plan and rollback criteria: (e.g., drop in pass-rate > 2 pp OR hallucination+toxicity flags > configured thresholds)
- Observability links: dashboard, traces, logs

B. Glossary
- Holdout: stable benchmark set reserved for regression detection.
- Canary: partial traffic deployment used to validate model in production.
- Quantization profile: configuration that maps FP weights to lower-precision representations.

C. Useful commands and snippets
- Run a single benchmark: `ri-eval run --config configs/benchmarks/qa-holdout.yaml --model-id {model}`
- Compare outputs: `ri-eval compare --baseline results/baseline --candidate results/candidate --metric hallucination_rate`
